Elena — quick technical note on the regression/eval approach so your audit team can vet our methodology:

Summary (TL;DR): we run layered checks at pre-release, canary, and production stages. Our regression pipeline blends seeded test suites with stratified live sampling and statistical hypothesis testing to detect distribution drift or metric regressions.

Key details:
- Sampling: stratified by customer segment, prompt type, and sequence length. Sample sizes chosen to target 95% power to detect a 2–3% change in primary metrics (e.g., correctness, hallucination rate) depending on baseline variability.
- Metrics: per-example and aggregate metrics include factual precision, instruction-following score, safety filter false-positive/negative rates, latency P50/P95/P99, and token-cost-per-response.
- Alerting and gating: we compute rolling windows (24h, 7d). Canary windows must show no statistically significant degradation on primary metrics (p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction across tests). If a regression is detected we: (a) pause traffic; (b) auto-fall back to last stable model variant; (c) create a regression ticket with trace IDs and sample set.
- Regression harness: reproducible job runs (CI) and an immutable snapshot of prompts/eval-seeds captured in eval_sample_manifest.csv (attached). We version-control evaluation sets and publish changelogs.

Attachment: eval_sample_manifest.csv (CSV — sample IDs, strata, baseline metrics)

Happy to walk through the math during the sync.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Evals, Redwood Inference
